docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Understand the structure of a good paragraph.
- Write a clear topic sentence, supporting sentences and a closing sentence.
- Link your ideas with connectors (and, but, because, so, then).
- Check and correct your own writing.

🔍 Warm-up
Read these two texts. Text A: "I like sport. Football. Every day. Good." Text B: "I really enjoy sport, especially football, because it keeps me healthy and I play every day after school." Which one is a real paragraph? This lesson shows you how to write like text B.

I. What a paragraph is
📘 Rule (writing)
A paragraph is a group of sentences about ONE main idea. A good paragraph has three parts:
1. A topic sentence: it introduces the main idea.
2. Supporting sentences: they give details, examples and reasons.
3. A closing sentence: it ends the paragraph or gives an opinion.

📏 Form (the shape of a paragraph)
- Start with a capital letter and, on paper, indent the first line.
- Write full sentences, one idea flowing into the next.
- End with a full stop.

👀 Note
A paragraph is NOT a list. Do not write single words or use bullet points. Join your ideas into flowing sentences.

II. The topic sentence
📘 Rule
The topic sentence tells the reader what the paragraph is about. It is usually the FIRST sentence and it is general.
✏️ Worked examples
- My best friend is a wonderful person.
- Last summer I had an unforgettable holiday.
- My town is a nice place to live.

🛠️ Method: writing a topic sentence
Step 1 — Decide your main idea (my hobby, my family, my holiday).
Step 2 — Write ONE general sentence that names the topic.
Step 3 — Keep it short and clear.

III. Supporting sentences and connectors
📘 Rule
Supporting sentences add details: who, what, where, when, why, how. To connect ideas smoothly we use linking words.
📏 Common connectors
- and: to add. I play tennis and I swim.
- but: to contrast. I like Maths, but I prefer English.
- because: to give a reason. I love it because it is fun.
- so: to give a result. It was late, so we went home.
- then / after that: to show order. First we ate, then we played.
- also / too: to add more. She sings. She also dances.

✏️ Worked example (topic + support)
My best friend is called Rania. She is thirteen and she lives near my house. She is kind and funny, so we laugh a lot together. We like the same things, because we both love reading and drawing. We often study together after school.

👀 Note
Vary your sentences. Do not begin every sentence with "I" or "She". Use connectors and different beginnings to make your writing interesting.

IV. The closing sentence
📘 Rule
The closing sentence rounds off the paragraph. It can repeat the main idea in other words, or give a feeling or opinion.
✏️ Worked examples
- That is why Rania is my best friend.
- I will never forget that wonderful holiday.
- I really love living in my town.

🛠️ Method: the full writing process
Step 1 — Brainstorm: write down ideas about your topic.
Step 2 — Plan: choose a topic sentence, three or four supporting ideas, and a closing sentence.
Step 3 — Write: turn your ideas into full sentences with connectors.
Step 4 — Check: read your paragraph and correct mistakes.

✏️ Model paragraph (topic: My favourite hobby)
My favourite hobby is photography. I started taking photos two years ago, when my father gave me an old camera. I love it because I can capture beautiful moments, such as sunsets and family celebrations. At the weekend I usually walk around my town and take pictures of interesting places. Then I show them to my friends, and they also enjoy them. Photography makes me happy, so I hope to become a professional photographer one day.

V. Checking your writing
📏 Checklist before you finish
1. Capital letters at the start of every sentence and for names.
2. A full stop at the end of every sentence.
3. Correct verb tenses (present for habits, past for finished actions).
4. Subject-verb agreement (he plays, they play).
5. Spelling of common words.
6. Connectors to link ideas.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Writing a list instead of sentences: "Football, swimming, every day." → full sentences.
2. No topic sentence: jumping straight into details.
3. Repeating "and... and... and..." too many times.
4. Forgetting capital letters and full stops.
5. Mixing tenses without reason.

⭐ Recap
- A paragraph is about ONE main idea.
- Structure: topic sentence + supporting sentences + closing sentence.
- Connect ideas with and, but, because, so, then, also.
- Follow the process: brainstorm, plan, write, check.
- Always check capitals, full stops, tenses and spelling.

📘 Language bank
Connectors: and, but, because, so, then, after that, also, too, first, finally.
Openers: My favourite..., Last summer..., I think that..., In my opinion...
Closers: That is why..., I will never forget..., I really love...
Useful sentences: My best friend is called Rania. / I love reading because it is relaxing. / First we visited the museum, then we had lunch. / In my opinion, sport is very important.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Put these sentences in the right order to make a paragraph.
a) That is why I love the sea so much.
b) My favourite place is the beach.
c) I also enjoy building sandcastles with my little brother.
d) I go there every summer with my family.
e) There, I can swim in the warm water and play games on the sand.

Exercise 2 — Choose the best connector (and, but, because, so, then).
1. I was tired, ______ I went to bed early.
2. I like tea, ______ I prefer coffee.
3. We visited the museum, ______ we had lunch.
4. She is happy ______ she passed her exam.

Exercise 3 — Write a short paragraph (topic sentence, two or three details, closing sentence) about your favourite hobby.

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: b, d, e, c, a.
Exercise 2: 1. so 2. but 3. then 4. because.

🗣️ Speaking task
Tell a partner your paragraph out loud before you write it. Speaking your ideas first helps you organise them and find the best connectors.

👀 Extra note
Never forget the shape of a good paragraph:
1. Topic sentence (the main idea).
2. Supporting sentences (details, examples, reasons with connectors).
3. Closing sentence (an opinion or feeling).
And always finish with the checklist: capital letters, full stops, correct tenses, correct spelling.

📋 Summary
- A paragraph is about ONE main idea and has three parts: a topic sentence, supporting sentences, and a closing sentence.
- The topic sentence is usually first and general; it names the main idea of the paragraph.
- Supporting sentences give details, examples and reasons, linked with connectors: and, but, because, so, then, also.
- The closing sentence rounds off the paragraph — it can repeat the idea or give an opinion.
- The writing process: brainstorm ideas, plan (topic + support + closing), write full sentences, then check.
- Always check capitals, full stops, correct tenses and spelling before finishing.
- A paragraph is never a list of words or bullet points — always write flowing, connected sentences.
